note: Save & Edit adds a 'Save & Edit' action to node add/edit forms (via save_edit_form_alter) that saves the node and redirects back to its edit-form, with optional auto-unpublish and default-button hiding. All behaviour is driven by the save_edit.settings config object: button_value, node_types (a bundle=>bundle-or-'0' map of which content types get the button), unpublish/unpublish_new_only, hide_default_save/publish/preview/delete, gin_primary. A content type is enabled when node_types.<bundle> === <bundle>. Introspection cases read live config (button label; which content type is enabled via a namespaced content type); execution cases enable Save & Edit on a namespaced content type and relabel + hide the default Save button, both verified against live config.

evals.prompt: What does the Save & Edit module add to node forms, and where does the site send the editor after they click its button?
evals.expected_output: It adds a 'Save & Edit' action button to node add/edit forms. After saving, save_edit_form_submit_redirect redirects to the entity's edit-form (rather than the default post-save page), preserving any destination param, so the editor stays on the edit form.

evals.prompt: How do I make the Save & Edit button appear for a particular content type, and what config controls that? What permission must the user have?
evals.expected_output: Enable the content type in save_edit.settings.node_types (a bundle=>bundle map; value equal to the bundle id means enabled, '0' means off), e.g. via /admin/config/save_edit/settings. The button also only appears for users with the 'use save and edit' permission.

evals.prompt: Can Save & Edit automatically unpublish a node when it is saved with its button, and which setting controls that behaviour only for newly created nodes?
evals.expected_output: Yes: the 'unpublish' setting auto-unpublishes on every Save & Edit save; 'unpublish_new_only' limits that to when the node isNew() (first save). Handled in save_edit_form_submit_presave.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Save & Edit button has been given a custom label. Inspect the live configuration and state the exact button text currently configured.
On this Drupal site, exactly one content type has the Save & Edit button enabled. Inspect the live save_edit configuration and give the machine name of that content type.

On this Drupal site there is a content type with machine name 'saveedit_task'. Using the Save & Edit module, configure it so the Save & Edit button appears on that content type's node forms. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: save_edit.settings.node_types.saveedit_task is set to 'saveedit_task' (value equal to the bundle id = enabled), e.g. drush cset save_edit.settings node_types.saveedit_task saveedit_task -y or via /admin/config/save_edit/settings.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Save & Edit so its button reads 'Save & Continue' and the default core Save button is hidden. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: save_edit.settings:button_value = 'Save & Continue' and hide_default_save = true (1), e.g. drush cset save_edit.settings button_value 'Save & Continue' -y and drush cset save_edit.settings hide_default_save 1 -y.
